name: manual_502211
claim: Handwaving a known error usually costs more later than fixing it now. When a check surfaces something that looks minor, tangential, or "not what I'm here to fix," the instinct to note it and move on is usually wrong -- the cost doesn't disappear, it just relocates to whoever hits it next (often the same agent, in a later, more expensive context). Treat every surfaced finding as either fixed now or explicitly, visibly deferred with a stated reason -- never silently absorbed into "I'll get to it."

decisions.notes: Directly requested this session, restated as the general principle behind several real findings that could have been waved off.
